To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stability of temporary screws is dependent on the cortical thickness and the presence of a cancellous layer, and that a cortical thickness of at least 2 mm is required for the stability of temporary screw.
temporary implants can be successfully inserted into cortical and cancellous bone, and that bone thickness is the main variable that influences the stability of temporary screw.
The cortical thickness and the presence of cancellous bone significantly influenced the stability of the temporary implant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of temporary implants with the aim to improve the stability of the implants during the healing phase.
the development of a new methodology for the evaluation of the stability of temporary screws.
the biomechanical aspects of temporary implants, which can be used in the design of new temporary implants and in the clinical practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability of the temporary screw is dependent on the cortical bone thickness.
the insertion torque and insertion strength of temporary screws are dependent on the cortical/cancelous thickness of the bone, which in turn is dependent on the type of the bone.
temporary screw insertion in cortical bone with a thickness of 2 mm or less is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cortical thickness and cancellous bone play a significant role in the insertion torque of self-drilling implants.
the insertion torque is directly proportional to cortical thickness.

the insertion of self-drilling screws into the cortical layer of the bone is not a critical step for temporary implants stability, and that the stability of the implants is mainly provided by the cancellous layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of the temporary implant can be modulated by the cortical/cancellus ratio and the cortical thickness.
the insertion torque and bone thickness can be used to predict the stability of temporary screws.
the insertion torque and insertion strength of temporary implants can be estimated by the cortical thickness and bone type.
